headline: That dial-up noise was two computers working out how to talk.
slides: First, a dial tone and the beeps of the number being dialled.
The other modem answers with a tone, and they start checking each other out.
The screeches are them testing the phone line and agreeing how fast they can go.
That final hiss of white noise usually meant you were in.
Modems played it out loud so you could hear if something went wrong, like someone picking up the phone.
It's one of the most recognisable sounds of the 90s.
